blocks.text: Some milestones arrive with fanfare. This one arrived quietly. The British Broadcasting Corporation (BBC) recently reported that the world now gets more electricity from the sun than from all its nuclear reactors combined. According to data from energy think tank Ember, solar generated a total of 2,807 terawatt-hours (TWh) over nuclear’s 2,805 TWh in 2025. From January to September 2026, solar has already produced 2,557 TWh, which is 24.5% more than nuclear’s 2,053 TWh and accounts for 10.63% of world electricity generation.
